note: Hebrew ah means brother or, broadly, relative; Jacob was Laban's nephew, so the literal "brother" misstates the relationship (likewise "my brother" in v.15).
Hebrew rakkot means soft or delicate; it is unclear whether it praises gentle eyes or marks a lack of lustre, but the contrast with Rachel's beauty suggests a shortcoming.
Hebrew senuah ("hated") is the idiom for the less-favoured wife (cf. Deut 21:15), as v.30 "loved Rachel more than Leah" shows; "hated" overstates it for a modern reader (also v.33).
